$comment: Beginner explainers shown in the app. Matthew owns this wording and edits it here; streams render it, never rewrite it. Drafts by Claude, Oct 7, 2026.

keyFinding.title: What's a key?
keyFinding.body: A key is a family of notes that all lean toward one home note. Hold the right home underneath and the melody sits comfortably on top of it; hold the wrong one and some notes rub against it, and that rub is the itch you'll hear.

keyGuess.$comment: What the key question says after a guess. {key} becomes the guess, like 'D major'. A demo tune knows its home, so its guesses get match or mismatch lines; other tunes get only 'chose'. Never name the tune's home.
keyGuess.match: That's the home most ears hear in this tune.
keyGuess.mismatch: Most ears hear home somewhere else in this tune. Listen to the last note over your home chord: does it settle, or hang?
keyGuess.otherMode: You're close: most ears hear this same home note, but hear the tune a little differently. Try it bright and dark, and listen to the last note: does it settle, or hang?
keyGuess.finderDifferent: Different from your earlier choice; your pick is now home.

voiceLeading.title: What's voice leading?
voiceLeading.body: Voice leading is how a pianist moves from one chord to the next with as little hand movement as possible: notes the two chords share stay put, often the home note, and the others step to the nearest key.
voiceLeading.off: Off: the chords around your choice hold still, so the only thing that changes is the chord you're testing. This is the clearest way to hear whether it fits.
voiceLeading.on: On: everything flows the way a pianist would play it. That can make a good choice sound even better, but it can also smooth over a weak one, so listen to the melody note: does it still sit comfortably on the chord?

options.$comment: One plain sentence per option, for newcomers, shown on hover and keyboard focus (src/toolbar/Tip.svelte). Drafts by Claude, Oct 7, 2026, for Matthew to edit.
options.roman: Roman numerals name each chord by its scale step, so the same pattern reads the same in any key. Example: I IV V.
options.nashville: Nashville numbers use plain numbers for the same idea, as session players do. Example: 1 4 5.
options.letters: Letters are the chord's actual name in this key. Example: C F G.
options.roman+letters: Both at once: the step from home, with the chord's actual name beside it. Example: I (C).
options.fromTop: Play plays the whole tune, from the first note to the last.
options.playKeys: Space: play from the top, pause, or resume. ←: back to the bar's start; ←← to the top.
options.pause: Pauses where it is. Resume picks up there; Stop goes back to the top.
options.resume: Resumes from the note where it paused.
options.stop: Stops playback and goes back to the top.
options.thisBar: Play plays only the bar of the note you last clicked. Click a note to choose the bar.
options.voiceLeading: Voice leading is how a pianist moves from one chord to the next with as little hand movement as possible. Off: only the chord you're testing changes. On: everything flows, which can flatter a weak choice.
options.drone: Holds the home chord under the tune while it plays, so you can hear which notes settle and which rub.
options.degrees: Shows each melody note's scale step under the staff, counted from home (1 is home).
options.bottomRowChords: The bottom row of letter keys plays chords, numbered from home.
options.bottomRowNotes: The bottom row of letter keys plays the scale's notes an octave below the number row.
options.undo: Takes back your last change. Cmd or Ctrl+Z.
options.redo: Puts back what you took back. Shift+Cmd or Ctrl+Z.
options.swing: Plays each pair of eighth notes long-short, the jazz feel. The notation stays in straight eighths.
options.words: Shows the song's words under the staff, one syllable per note.
options.more: Less common actions, like printing the lead sheet.
options.print: Prints the tune as a lead sheet: the staff with its chord symbols.
